text:
Alex K: FYI seeing a spike of DNS timeouts from GPU pods in us-west-2c-3 since ~09:12 UTC, internal svc->svc calls failing with upstream failures (pods hit 5xx).
Marta P: I can see the same in traces — tail latency for resolve jumps and then downstream request retries pile up. Any recent network changes?
Alex K: No config changes on the app side. Pod restarts correlate with resolve errors. Kernel logs show a lot of ICMP frag-needed around that time.
Jordan L: ICMP frag-needed = MTU problem. Are we still mixing 9000/1500 MTU across hosts and RDMA fabric?
Li Wei: Yes, GPU racks use RDMA with jumbo frames (9000). Some compute hosts on the new AZ came up with default 1500 on the CNI overlay.
Marta P: That explains fragmentation of DNS UDP packets — fragments frequently drop and CoreDNS gets truncated queries -> SERVFAIL.
Alex K: Sample tcpdump from a failing pod (truncated):
```
10:12:34.123456 IP pod-ip.54321 > coredns.svc.cluster.local.53: 512+ A? registry.svc.cluster.local. (36)
10:12:34.123456 IP (frag 1) pod-ip > coredns  UDP, length 512
10:12:34.123457 IP (frag 2) pod-ip > coredns  UDP, length 480
```
Jordan L: If frag 2 gets dropped, the resolver will timeout. Node-local-dns caches may not help if they see the truncated requests.
sre-bot: alert: dns-error-rate: us-west-2c GPU pool — 4.8% error rate over 5m (threshold 1.0%).
Li Wei: Quick mitigation: force DNS over TCP for node-local-dns / CoreDNS between nodes? DNS over TCP reduces frag issues but increases latency/conn overhead.
Marta P: We should also try a two-prong approach: 1) short-term: configure node-resolver fallback to CoreDNS via TCP for pods with high QPS, or increase the node-local cache TTL to reduce churn; 2) medium-term: normalize MTU across the AZ and ensure CNI allows jumbo frames end-to-end for RDMA racks.
Alex K: How invasive is forcing TCP for DNS? Any kube-proxy/netfilter gotchas?
Jordan L: CoreDNS supports tcp. For kubelet/resolv.conf, we can add `options single-request-reopen` but that's for glibc DNS behavior. For forcing TCP from coredns->upstream, set `forward` plugin with `tls`/`transport`? Simpler: enable `proxy` or `tcp` in the node-local-dns config so it retries via TCP on UDP failure.
Li Wei: We tested a quick node-local-dns patch on one node: set `upstreamTransport: tcp` for high qps namespaces — DNS error rate dropped from 4.8% -> 0.6% for that node, app latency improved.
Marta P: Good. I'll open a small rollout to the other GPU nodes and also add iptables conntrack logging to validate fragment drops.
Alex K: Can we also add a short-term iptables rule to bypass overlay for DNS (host-network) on node-local-dns pods so fragmentation path is simpler?
Jordan L: HostNetwork for node-resolver makes sense, but be careful with port collisions. Also, we should avoid using public DNS fallbacks (8.8.8.8) for internal svc names.
Li Wei: Agreed. I'm scheduling MTU normalization tomorrow morning (low usage window) — will coordinate k8s rolling restart on those AZ nodes.
Marta P: Notes for the runbook I'll add: check `ip -s link`, verify `ethtool -k` for offloads, tcpdump for `ip[6] & 0x1fff != 0` (fragmented flag), and monitor `coredns` logs for `truncated`/`SERVFAIL`.
Alex K: Thanks team — rolling the TCP fallback and hostNetwork change now. Ping me if anything spikes. :thumbsup:
